x: Incidentally, the "Berman" Cup had been allocated, by kind permission of the R.W.A., to our event, and this win—our third in succession—made the trophy the Club's own property. Bill True (10 min. 30 sec. allowance) won the handicap event, with A.
Little, Ted Elliott and Bill True. We believe the latter is somewhere in Dorset.
Says the sand is an excellent substitute for the Wimbledon mud. Bill True, a "lost contact," has turned up. He is now a corporal in R.A.C., stationed not too far from London, and looks very well.
Bill True is still at Sandhurst. He met with an accident in a tank, but has since recovered.
Bill True is still with the R.A.C., O.C.T.U., Sandhurst, and always pays us a visit when in town. Charlie Smart is now over the water with the B.L.A.
Bill True is still busy at Sandhurst, but was able to visit us and turn out at the Open Walk. Laurie Jackson is still undergoing treatment and is having a skin grafting at the back of his knee.

Bert Webb and George Bentley, who had walked together almost throughout, maintained their positions at 4th and 5th and after Bill True and Don Heath had been told of the loss of East, they both got down to it and succeeded in carrying our team into 2nd position.
George Beecham won the 2 miles walk handicap with our old friend Harry Shields battling away to gain 2nd place from Bill True, the handicapper!
Childs taking first prize in the Discus handicap, while George Oliver won the 2 miles walk handicap with Bill True second and George Beecham third.
To round off the evening they held a walking race over 1 mile and Bill True came along to take part, but do not think he was very impressed.

Looked after and urged on by a grand bunch of supporters - Bob Newson, Len Demmon, Billy True - they consolidated their positions and the scoring four of Mac, Norman, Bernard and Harry were ably backed up by George Checkley, George Beecham, Joe Wilson, Gordon Doubleday and Fred Rolfe, finishing posi…
There were 13 starters and our handicapper, Bill True, with a time of 62m.57s (all.7.15) was second in the handicap with Pot Hunter Harry Shields 3rd.
Logan, 17 minutes and 3rd none other than the Handicapper, Bill True off 11.30. The match resulted in a win for Belgrave by 104 points to 149.
Could Eric and Syd continue their good form, and what of George Beecham, Maurice Nye, Bill True and Doub, who was going to make up the team.

Harry after a not very good day, finished 27th with evergreen Bob Readman 42nd, Bill True 49th, Syd Spencer 63rd and Cyril Yescombe 66th. Since this event Cyril has shown considerable improvement and looks like being an asset to the team next year.
Len Demmon trailed the Captain home in 3.13.13 with Bob Readman and Bill True just behind, followed by Cyril Yescombe continuing to show improvement.
3rd Bill True.

During the journey home, whether it was due to the over-excitement as a result of the victory or the cold, certainly nothing else for we hsd not then stopped, Bill True passed out and we came to a halt miles from anywhere whilst he was resuscitated with fresh air.

Fred Rolfe, walking as an individual, enjoyed a race without team cares and grateful words of thanks and honourable mention go to Jack Goswell, Stan Vickers and Bill True who did what they could at the roadside for our walkers.
Bill True is making note of the result in case you continue walking on your return to this country.
The handicap was won by Bill True.
Congrats to you both; says he has retired from running as he finds he's too old at 28! whew! BILL TRUE is still at Sandhurst. He met with an accident in a tank, but has since recovered.
Bill True, S.W.17
